prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: It depends on what you want to do in Branson.

- Pick a hotel if you want convenience, consistent service (daily housekeeping, front desk, on-site restaurants/pools), easy booking/cancellation, or if you’re traveling with kids and want amenities like indoor waterparks.
- Pick an Airbnb (or a private cabin) if you want more space, a kitchen, a quieter/“local” vibe, lakefront access, or you’re traveling with a larger group and want to split the cost.

Which to choose — guidance by traveler type
- Families with kids who want pools/activities: hotel/resort (or family-oriented condo complex) on/near Highway 76 (the Strip).
- Couples wanting a romantic getaway: lakefront cabin/Airbnb or upscale resort on Table Rock Lake.
- Groups or multi-family trips: larger Airbnb or cabin with multiple bedrooms and a kitchen.
- Theater/Strip-focused visitors: a hotel on the 76 Strip or near the Branson Landing for short drives/walking to shows and dining.
- Visiting Silver Dollar City: stay closer to West Branson or near Highway 165 (shorter drive), many cabins/Airbnbs work well.

Specific highly-regarded options (by type)
Hotels / Resorts
- Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — upscale, lakefront, full-service spa and nice lake views. Great for romantic or luxury stays.
- Big Cedar Lodge (nearby in Ridgedale) — premium lodge-style resort on Table Rock Lake with outdoor activities, golf, marina; excellent if you want a resort experience and nature.
- Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — excellent if you want to be right at Branson Landing (shops, restaurants, riverfront) and an easy walk to downtown attractions.
- Family-friendly Strip hotels (examples to search): Grand Country Inn & Waterpark, and several mid-range chains on Highway 76 — convenient to shows and attractions.
- The Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks — unique, well-reviewed lodge experience with high standards and on-site dining; quieter and a short drive to the Strip.

Airbnb / Cabin types to search for
- Table Rock Lake cabins with private docks — great for boating, fishing, sunset views and quiet evenings.
- Mountain/Ozarks cabins near Silver Dollar City — good for families who want a multi-night park focus.
- Condos or lofts at Branson Landing — walkable location, often with river views and easy access to dining/shops.
- Large vacation homes on/near Highway 76 — good for groups who want to be close to shows but have shared living/kitchen space.

Practical tips for choosing/booking
- Location matters: the Strip (76) is busiest with theaters and family attractions; Branson Landing is walkable and scenic; Table Rock Lake is quieter and more outdoorsy. Map drive times to your planned activities.
- Book early for spring and summer and peak show seasons (weekends and holidays) — especially for cabins and popular hotels.
- Compare total cost: some Airbnbs add cleaning and service fees and hotels may add resort/parking fees.
- Read recent reviews for cleanliness and host responsiveness on Airbnb, and check if hotels have on-site amenities you need (indoor pool, waterpark, spa, free parking).
- If you need accessibility or pet-friendly lodging, filter specifically — not all cabins or hotels accommodate these needs.

If you tell me:
- dates,
- number of people,
- budget per night,
- and what you most want (shows, lake, family activities, quiet getaway),

I can recommend specific available hotels or Airbnb listings and compare prices/drive times. Which are your travel dates and priorities?
